name: tests-half-octodns-processor-record-lineage-across-planning
instr:
octoDNS cannot currently audit how source records become, or fail to become, provider changes. Add opt-in lineage through mutation, copying, hydration, aggregation, filtering, and planning without changing ordinary behavior.

Make `ProcessorContext` importable from `octodns.processor.context`.

`ProcessorContext`, `RecordOrigin`, `LineageStep`, and `RecordLineage` must isolate each zone run and target. Origins must survive copies and replacements independently of object identity. `for_target(self, target_id)`, `trace(self, record)`, `report(self)`, `derive(self, processor_id, hook, original, result)`, `suppress(self, processor_id, hook, record)`, `aggregate(self, processor_id, hook, origins, result)`, and `failure(self, processor_id, hook, record, error)` record ordered transformations and failures. Report suppressed records once in hook order, never as zone records or provider changes.

ACME, AutoArpa, type, name, value, network, root-NS and zone-name filters, TTL clamping, ownership, meta, restriction, and SPF must preserve existing outcomes and report exact ancestry for actual transformations. Do not record mutations for unchanged records. ACME must distinguish marker insertion from target suppression, trace owned replacements to the original TXT record and marker across lifecycle hooks, retain source-owned target challenges, and report unmanaged target removal without inventing a source origin. TTL clamps must trace original and clamped values.

Reports must follow proces
